title: Volume 2 Chapter 2: The Sister Cries, the Flames Do Not, and the Dagger Remains Unbroken 3
content: And if we succeed, then from the Church's perspective, they have nothing to lose.
Honestly, my first thought is that they've been outsmarted.
But at the same time, I can't help but wonder what kind of expressions they'll have when we successfully accomplish this request from the Church.
"Who would hesitate to walk the common path...?"
As I muttered Erika's words from some time ago while returning a book to the shelf, I noticed Erika and Shara looking at me.
Erika wore a satisfied smile, while Shara had a look of disbelief.
"That's right, my dear husband," Erika said with a fierce grin.
There’s no common path leading deep into the Demon Realm,
" Shara said with a face that looked like she was about to cry.
Erika Solnzali was truly enjoying herself.
Having a goal was incredibly enjoyable, especially when that goal was one she could set for herself.
This is freedom.
Making Shin into an adventurer of the appropriate rank was a goal I had almost decided on a whim.
But now that goal had transformed into something serious.
"Hey, wait, Shara. Don't try to buy food. We're going to eat now, okay?"
The boy, clearly not suited for the adventurer rank he held, sighed while grabbing the collar of the blonde sister.
"That grilled meat over there is really delicious, you know?"
Is that so? So that grilled meat is indeed delicious.
Erika added "buying food from a stall" to the top of her list of things she wanted to do.
She had been curious about that stall for a while.
"Are you a child? How can you..."
The words Shin swallowed were probably, "How can you still be a spy for the Church?"
Though we had only known each other for a short time, I could tell something.
Shin Longdagger was the kind of person who said things clearly at times like this.
The fact that he swallowed his words meant—Erika thought—he must also have a good impression of Shara, just like I did.
He had been doing something unbefitting a bishop in front of the bishop, but Erika couldn't help but smile at the memory.
His eyes spoke volumes.
More than words or expressions, his eyes conveyed everything.
He seemed to be aware of it, and when he tried to act like a husband in front of me, he seemed to consciously try to appear
"husband-like.
I thought that was something he needed to be a bit more careful about.
Even though I understood, my heart raced a little.
I was glad that Shin was an honest person.
If he had been careless with women, he would have turned out to be a rather bad man.
"Grilled meat is good for tired eyes! Probably!"
"Don't say probably!"
Shin, with a face like an older brother scolding a younger sister, looked amusing.
As for me... well, to put it simply, I didn't like that Shin was being underestimated.
That's why I spoke proudly when talking to the bishop.
I don't think I exaggerated, but it was definitely with pride.
Having been the daughter of a high noble, Erika had some confidence in her ability to read the room, and she felt no malice from the bishop's attitude.
At the very least, they were watching us but probably had no intention of doing anything right away.
So Erika boasted about Shin to her heart's content.
She bragged that her husband was amazing.
Regardless of the Church's intentions behind the request for a mission to the Demon Realm, Erika thought they should boast about Shin’s greatness to the Adventurer Guild.
She never once considered that they might fail.
As long as she was with Shin, she couldn't imagine failure.
However, there was a problem that was more pressing than imagining failure.
For some reason, both the adventurers and the guild were reacting "slowly."
Why did no one understand?
When she spoke about the time they defeated the Forest Dragon, everyone fell silent.
Even the bishop did.
No matter how amazing Shin was, when she talked about it, everyone would think for a moment and then ultimately look away.
Why was that?
Even the adventurers, including those who had witnessed the defeat of the Forest Dragon right in front of them, wore the same expression.
Erika recalled the female adventurers she had drunk with during the
"We defeated the Forest Dragon!
Let's celebrate!
" party.
When they asked about Shin and she bragged to her heart's content, they all had expressions like, "Really? Seriously?"
What was going on?
Thinking back, she also disliked the nickname that Shin had been given.
What does "unfitting for his status" even mean?
She knew there was no malice behind it, but whether she could accept it was another matter.
She thought there had to be something better.
Like "Swift Longdagger" or "Indomitable Longdagger."
Something more fitting.
Why was it "unfitting for his status"?
...No, perhaps the nickname itself was unfitting for him?
If that's the case, then the namer had quite the sense.
After all, the Adventurer Guild was the guild.
She thought they should just make him rank 7 as an exception.
What on earth was the problem?
It was unacceptable.
She absolutely had to raise Shin's adventurer rank quickly.
And then she would brag, "My husband is amazing."
No, no, that's not it.
What am I saying?
I want Shin to be aware of his own abilities, so I want to raise his adventurer rank.
It’s definitely not about wanting to brag.
After all, that person is in the same wilderness as me—
At that moment, Erika realized she had stopped and was deep in thought.
When she involuntarily looked up with a wry smile, her eyes met those of Shin and Shara.
What was that expression?
Both of them had faces that suggested they had something difficult to say.
"Um... Erika?"
What is it?
Erika tilted her head towards Shara.
"That stall is always open, you know."
—Huh?
Erika was about to ask what she meant when she realized she had been standing in front of the grilled meat stall, deep in thought.
She almost let out a scream.
No, that's not it; it's a misunderstanding.
"Next time, let's eat there."
When even Shin started saying such things, Erika shouted.
As a lady, she couldn't care less about raising her voice.
"That's not it! That's not it!? I was certainly curious about it before!"
Erika protested vehemently to the two, who were inexplicably smiling gently.
After spending a day in the guild's library, the only thing we discovered was that we knew nothing.
Of course, there was useful information, such as the location of the Church built in the Demon Realm, but all of it was outdated, and there was no information about the current situation.
The old maps included paths to the Church in the Demon Realm, but since it was the Demon Realm, there was no doubt that those paths no longer existed.
The fact that there was only old information clearly indicated the extent of the tragedy that forced humanity to retreat from the Demon Realm they had once opened up.
Losing many excellent adventurers meant losing the next generation of excellent adventurers.
Hekatai, having lost many skilled adventurers who took on apprentices and nurtured the next generation, had yet to recover from that blow.
The boundary between the Demon Realm and the human territory, having significantly retreated from its peak, serves as proof of that.
"What are we going to do from here?"
Shara asked, her overworked eyes squinting.
As I pondered how to respond, I took a sip of water from a wooden cup.
We were in an adventurer's cafeteria, a perfect place for the adventurers who had finished their work to discuss the Church's matters amidst a pleasant noise.
"Even if we sift through the materials, we won't know the current state of the Demon Realm," I said.
If we were to properly accomplish the request, we would have to start by gathering information about the Demon Realm ourselves, taking our time.
Normally, it would take several months to prepare for a journey to the Church in the Demon Realm.
But the Church wouldn't allow that.
They would surely come up with some reason to rush us.
That's true.
In that case, we should take our time to gather information about the Demon Realm with our own eyes and prepare,
" Shara said.
See? They’re rushing us… huh?
I was surprised by Shara's very reasonable statement and couldn't help but stare at her.
Shara tilted her head slightly.
"What is it?"
"Well... I thought you would say we should move to reclaim it as quickly as possible."
"Even I don't think this request will end easily. We should spend at least a few months just on the investigation."
I was taken aback by Shara's obvious and reasonable words.
What was she thinking?
Did the Church want to take its time for some reason?
I couldn't understand.
But I should take this as a good opportunity.
I didn't know the Church's intentions, but I could just go along with it.
Just as I was about to voice my agreement, I heard a familiar voice.
"What are you talking about?"
A sense of dread rose within me.
That voice belonged to Erika.
It was the same tone she used when she received inquiries from underclassmen and classmates at the academy.
"Even if we spend tomorrow preparing, we will enter the Demon Realm the day after tomorrow, you know?"
—Huh?
Shara let out a voice that sounded like she had just heard a bad joke.
She then opened her mouth to speak but hurriedly closed it, perhaps because the words that almost came out were,
"Are you serious?
It was wise of her to stop before it came out.
Erika Solnzali had this tendency.
Sometimes she became oblivious to the fact that she was in the category of geniuses.
This manifested in various ways, such as unconsciously expecting the same level of understanding from others or evaluating magic and swordsmanship based on her own standards.
What was generally common was that when Erika behaved this way, it was when she held the other person in high regard.
In this case, it was probably because the recent subjugations had gone well consecutively.
But that was a misunderstanding.
Whether it was the Golden Ogre, the Forest Dragon, or that assassin who had transformed into a demon.
The only reason they had come out unscathed was because Erika was there.
That high evaluation, which did not take that into account, was likely the reason for Erika's statement.
However, denying that high evaluation here would be a bad move.
I wanted to ask why, truly why.
When Erika reached this state, she wouldn't easily change that evaluation.
As a result, I had seen many times at the academy how those who were highly evaluated were crushed by expectations.
As far as I knew, only the Light Priestess had withstood Erika's high evaluation attack.
This was the greatest barrier between what was commonly known as Erika's wall and the priestess.
However, this time, we were in the mid-level of the Demon Realm.
It wasn't as if we had just had a good exam score or that our magic or swordsmanship was exceptional.
With a wrong evaluation, nothing serious would happen because Erika was there, but it was still dangerous.
I had to clear up this misunderstanding—
"After all, Shin is here, you know?"
I closed my mouth.
"I also claim to be somewhat capable. With us, the mid-level of the Demon Realm is nothing to fear."
Isn't that right?
As Erika smiled at me, I silently nodded in agreement.
What kind of husband would I be if I didn't fulfill my wife's wishes?
That wish was something a little life-threatening.
No, sorry, I lied a little.
I silently apologized to Shara.
...See, I'm a boy too.
I want to show off in front of the girl I like.
I gently averted my gaze from Shara, who was frozen with a desperate expression.
In the city of Hekatai, a rank 5 adventurer named Barrel heard a strange rumor that day.
It seemed that the Longdagger Couple had received a request from the Church to search for something deep in the mid-level of the Demon Realm, in the depths of the forest.
When Barrel heard that rumor, he thought that it was normal for those two to receive a request from the Church even at rank 1.
What was strange was that everyone who spoke of that rumor all said, "This is just between us," and so on.
The fact that adventurers were talking about it as a rumor meant it was not just between them.
But that also revealed something.
At the very least, the Church wanted to keep it "just between us."
The relationship between the Church and adventurers was deep.
Adventurers would go to the Church to have their injuries healed, and in the name of helping the weak, the Church would send its people to assist adventurers.
Sometimes, they would act faster than the Adventurer Guild and directly request adventurers to deal with troublesome monsters that appeared in remote villages.
By the way, the Church has people who are stronger than average adventurers, so when the Church asks for help from adventurers, it usually means they are in a troublesome situation.
Those who are asked often end up making a face full of reluctance.
Moreover, since they are indebted to the Church, it is hard to refuse.
Barrel thought that the request to the Longdagger Couple was of that nature.
Those two had a sister dispatched from the Church, and because of that relationship, they likely ended up receiving a troublesome request related to the Church.
Well, those two were so outrageous that they could handle anything. Barrel wasn't worried.
After all, he had just seen those two beat the Forest Dragon to death.
It made no sense.
Especially the husband; he was truly incomprehensible.
He fought while being mindful of stray bullets hitting other adventurers.
At one point, to avoid involving other adventurers, he took the dragon's claw head-on, with his stomach.
And then he got angry because his clothes got torn and crushed the dragon's head, which made no sense at all.
In the adventurer's profession, where self-responsibility is the norm, the one who got caught up in it is at fault.
If he was furious about his clothes getting torn, he should have been angry at the foolish adventurer first.
Ah, could it be?
Barrel chuckled at the possibility that suddenly came to mind.
"He might just have wanted to look good in front of his wife."
Before rank 5 adventurer Barrel faced hell, it was early morning.
"This is it."
He said while spreading out a copy of an old map and checking the compass and the old stone signpost that looked like it would crumble at any moment.
Before him lay a deep, dark forest.
The edge of the forest known as the mid-level of the Demon Realm.
"According to the map and the signpost, if we head north from here, we should reach the Church."
When I said that, the two of them wore contrasting expressions.
Erika looked like a climber gazing up at a mountain worth climbing, while Shara had a face that still couldn't decide if this was a joke or a nightmare.
Unfortunately, this was reality.
We were indeed standing in this place after just one day's preparation, as Erika had declared.
It was an unbelievable preparation time, but the grasslands of the Demon Realm were certainly easy to traverse since they were shallow layers.

During the day, the grassland was filled with many adventurers, meaning it was a place suitable for many adventurers to earn a quick buck, so it was no surprise that it turned out that way with Erika around.
However, from here on out, it was the mid-level.
Considering that the forest of the Demon Realm had not been cleared, it was clear that even in Hekatai, a town of adventurers, there were few adventurers who could operate in the mid-level.
The forest of the Demon Realm apparently withers when the number of surrounding monsters decreases.
In other words, the adventurers of Hekatai could defeat monsters to the extent that the mid-level forest wouldn't expand, but they couldn't defeat enough monsters to push the forest back.
We were about to head into a forest teeming with such monsters.
To be honest, I wanted to say we should stop even now... but yeah, that's impossible.
I gave up when I looked at Erika's face, which was completely motivated.
The mid-level of the Demon Realm, the forest of the Demon Realm welcomed us with a fitting reception.
Within an hour of entering the forest, monsters attacked us from all directions.
There were many of them; as expected of the Demon Realm.
I cut down three monsters that jumped at me from the front.
I must not let my guard down.
"Is it okay to say this?"
I should... "The mid-level of the Demon Realm is surprisingly boring, Shin."
I must not let my guard down!

I reminded myself not to let my guard down while watching the monsters that were set ablaze by Erika the moment they entered her range, whether in the air, on the ground, underground, in the trees, or in the shadows.
By the way, Shara was looking at Erika with a "What is this person saying?" expression.
I thought she was gradually losing her reservations.
"Well... to be honest, I can't say I didn't think it would be like this, but it is the Demon Realm."
I hesitated to admit it but responded to Erika.
I felt the same way as Erika.
Shara was looking at me with a similar expression.
No, because honestly, I truly felt that way.
When I stepped into the famous mid-level of the Demon Realm, I expected to face something formidable, but all that came out were numerous weaklings.
It wasn't that Erika and I were abnormal; if it were like this, rank 4 adventurers from the Faltarl Kingdom would gladly hunt monsters here.
Even a party of rank 3 adventurers with good coordination would be fine.
In other words, for now, it was at that level.
Indeed, it was true that Erika's presence made it this easy.
After all, the moment most monsters entered her range, they were set ablaze.
Honestly, it made no sense.
Rather, Erika made far more sense than the Demon Realm.
As soon as she stepped into the forest, she said, "Oh, it seems I've gained a skill."
Was this her sense of presence?
That was her impression.
As for my impression, if she called this sense of presence, I wanted to ask what kind of skill my sense of presence was.
Erika's self-proclaimed sense of presence was of abnormal precision.
Not only was the precision abnormal, but she claimed it also worked underground, so I wanted to say that it definitely wasn't a sense of presence.
I had never heard of such a sense of presence skill.
While my range was broad but vague, the fact that she could detect even when the opponent was trying to hide their presence set her abilities apart entirely from mine.
What was even more abnormal was that Erika had only gained that skill less than an hour ago.
Yet, here she was.
I felt like sighing as I watched the monsters that exceeded my sense of presence being set ablaze by Erika's magic.
It was painful to see the person I liked being so much of a genius.
Being able to use a skill and mastering it are not the same thing.
Just as the sense of presence used by a seasoned scout is entirely different from my sense of presence, there is a significant difference between being able to use something and mastering it.
Erika, that extraordinary genius, was naturally mastering a skill she had just acquired.
As she illuminated the dim forest with her golden magical power, she walked through the forest of the Demon Realm with an almost arrogant confidence.
As her husband, I at least wanted to keep up with her.
Even a moth diving into the flame would think a bit more.
But I had no reason not to follow Erika.
If I believed the map and the records of the time, the location of the Church in the Demon Realm should be about a day's walk from where we entered the forest.
For a typical adventurer who could use physical enhancement, it would take about three hours.
For high-rank adventurers, if I were to say arrogantly, Erika and I could shorten that time even further.

But that was merely a matter of distance; since we were actually traversing through the forest of the Demon Realm, we would likely have to fight monsters, and I thought it would be impossible to do it in such a short time.
So...
"I was thinking that," I said, realizing a hint of exasperation had crept into my voice.
"W-What do you mean?"
Shara replied dutifully to my words, which I had intended as a monologue.
She was panting because she had matched our pace.
She could have just silently caught her breath, but she seemed either earnest or dutiful.
"What do you think this is?"
I pointed at the ground.
"Um... a rock?"
I couldn't help but chuckle at Shara's answer.
At least until her breath steadied and her mind cleared, we would take a break.
I silently asked Erika to keep watch around us and then taught Shara the correct answer.
"It's a signpost that says we're about an hour's walk from the Church."
Shara smiled broadly.
She had a face that seemed to say, "Oh come on, you're joking! I won't be fooled!"
"Look," I said, stepping aside a half-step so she could see the signpost better.
It was covered in moss, cracked, and looked like it would crumble at any moment due to the environment of the Demon Realm.
But it was undoubtedly a signpost, with the emblem of the city of Hekatai and the number assigned to the signpost barely visible.
"Isn't this real?"
For some reason, Shara scolded me.
"This! I saw it on the map yesterday!"
Pointing at the barely readable number on the signpost, Shara shouted.
I understood why she felt like shouting.
I hadn't expected the exploration of the Demon Realm to progress at this speed.

Indeed, Erika's performance was nothing short of incredible, but even she didn't have an inexhaustible supply of magical power, so I had thought it would be impossible to continue advancing while defeating that many monsters, and we would have to consider retreating at some point.
I never thought we would reach the Church in the Demon Realm on the first day, but after moving for a while, the monsters suddenly stopped appearing.
Even with my broad but vague sense of presence, I could tell that the presence of monsters had drastically decreased.
There wasn't even a single monster that entered Erika's range.
Rather than saying there were none, it seemed that the monsters were fleeing as we approached.
It was quite a rare phenomenon.
Monsters are generally beings that attack when they spot a person.
For them to avoid us... as expected of Erika.
Erika was amazing.
It was a situation that made me wonder what had happened to the swarm of monsters right after we entered the forest.
What was even more concerning was that we hadn't encountered any other adventurers.
This was the forest known as the mid-level, but it had also been a place cleared by humanity in the past.
It didn't make sense that we hadn't met a single adventurer by the time we got this far.
Even if the number of adventurers had decreased since their heyday, it was unreasonable that there were no adventurers making a living in the mid-level.
In fact, the mid-level should be the main area for adventurers to earn money; yet, it felt as if...
It felt as if someone was clearing the area of people.
Well, there shouldn't be any reason for that... right?
In that instant, a thought flashed through my mind, and at almost the same time, I felt a huge chill.
I regretted being confused only after realizing I had lost a precious moment.
